To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a cable driven redundant manipulator can be controlled by a joint space controller that is capable of satisfying stringent positioning requirements, despite the inherent limitations of task space pose measurements.

(i) the proposed control topology for the joint space controller is suitable for the KNTU cable driven redundant parallel robot and it can be applied to other redundant parallel manipulators; and (ii) the joint space controller has the ability to track desired trajectories in the workspace of the robot.
The KNTU CDPRM can be successfully controlled in the singular free workspace with the proposed joint space control topology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new control architecture for the KNTU Cable Driven Redundant Parallel Manipulator, which is capable to track a desired trajectory, while the cables are always kept in tension.

the control of the CDRPM, with the aim of providing a controller which is capable of tracking desired trajectories in a large and free singular workspace, while guaranteeing that the cables are under tension at all times.
the development and implementation of control strategies for cable-driven parallel mechanisms.

this paper presents a new control topology, which is capable to guarantee that all cables of the KNTC CDRPM are always under tension, and the tracking errors are bounded, despite the inherent limitations of task space pose measurements.
the proposed control topology is able to fulfill all the stringent requirements for the KNTU-CDRPM, while being able to handle the inherent redundancy and the singular workspace of the manipulator.
the proposed control topology for the KNTU-CDRPM can guarantee the required tracking performance and cable tension in a large free and singular workspace.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed control topology is capable to guarantee the tracking of the desired trajectory, while the cables are always in tension.
the controller is capable to fulfill its goals in a large free workspace and the proposed control topology is capable to satisfy stringent positioning requirements.
the proposed joint-space control topology is a promising approach for the control of cable-driven redundant parallel manipulators, which can also be extended to other cable-driven manipulators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the joint space control topology can be used to control the CDRPM, despite the fact that the forward kinematics are implicit.
it is possible to control the CDRPM without any task space pose measurement, and the proposed control topology can guarantee the tension in all cables.
a simple joint space controller is enough to guarantee a good tracking performance for a cable driven parallel manipulator.
